task: Correct the v1 batch-length turnaround accrual mechanism so it delays the REVERSE-ACK ARRIVAL via the turnaround GAP (keyed to the FORWARD a2b OFDM batch airtime), leaving the forward OFDM bit-exact. Env-gated, default-off byte-identical. Failing-test-first.

v1_mechanism_error_corrected.diagnosis: The v1 accrual (sim_channel_relay.py v1 lines 678-717) added the one-sided LATE offset to EACH DIRECTION's OWN just-ended burst (self.cur_burst_samples) and spent it at THAT SAME instance's next signal ONSET by inserting silence AHEAD of the burst (v1 lines 705-712). The forward (a2b OFDM) and reverse (b2a MFSK ACK) directions are SEPARATE TurnaroundDrift instances (main: turn['a2b']/turn['b2a']), so the long FORWARD batch accrued ~6608 samp and inserted it INTO the forward OFDM signal -> de-aligned the forward decode (relay ins=90313 samp/286 ms; FTR-FAIL x414, SKIP-VAR x116, 3-consec-abort x31, metric->0.12-0.25, proc_died; held-CFG16 ~1897 bps, 3.2x too optimistic vs bench-9 597.6).
v1_mechanism_error_corrected.hw_mechanism_modeled: bench-9: the CMD finishes its FORWARD a2b OFDM batch, drops PTT, opens its receive window; keyer/AGC/capture-flush/scheduling latency accumulated DURING the forward batch makes the REVERSE b2a MFSK ACK arrive LATE at the CMD in proportion to the FORWARD batch airtime, landing OUTSIDE the CMD receiving_timeout window -> matched=0/7 -> D3 reverse-ACK-starvation -> active 18.9%, whole-window 597.6. Calibration constant 30 ms/s (firmware common_defines.h:589).

fix.mechanism: CROSS-DIRECTION coupling via a shared TurnaroundCoupler. Each TurnaroundDrift PUBLISHES its just-ended forward-burst airtime to the coupler on its signal->silence FALLING edge (burst end), and CONSUMES the OTHER direction's pending forward airtime at its OWN silent->signal ACK ONSET, adding accrual_ms_per_s * forward_burst_s of one-sided LATE offset to its acc. The existing silence-onset insert then delays THIS direction's ACK signal onset by inserting silence in its turnaround GAP. So the LONG forward a2b OFDM batch pushes the SHORT reverse b2a MFSK ACK late (the bench-9 collapse) while the FORWARD OFDM signal is NEVER touched: the forward instance only PUBLISHES; it CONSUMES only the tiny reverse-ACK airtime, realized harmlessly in its own gap.
fix.key_difference_from_v1: v1 accrued a direction's OWN burst into its OWN onset (self-accrual) -> silence into the forward signal. v2 accrues the OTHER direction's forward-burst airtime (consumed from the shared coupler) -> silence only into the reverse ACK's turnaround gap.
fix.gating: OPT-IN: --turnaround-batch-accrual OR env MERCURY_SIM_BATCH_ACCRUAL=1; requires --turnaround-drift. accrual_ms_per_s defaults to 0.0 in the TurnaroundDrift ctor; with accrual off NOTHING publishes so consume() always returns 0 -> the legacy per-direction model is byte-identical for every existing caller.
